newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin names surgeon, venue for Yeltsin's op.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin names surgeon, venue for Yeltsin's op.

text.p: The Kremlin said on Monday that Russian surgeon Renat Akchurin would lead bypass heart surgery on President Boris Yeltsin and a bulletin on the president's health would be released later in the day.
A presidential spokesman said the operation would take place at Moscow's Cardiology Research Centre.
A council of doctors, including Akchurin and U.S. expert Michael DeBakey, was meeting on Monday to decide whether Yeltsin was fit for surgery, he said.
Yevgeny Chazov, head of the Cardiology Centre, and Sergei Mironov, head of the Kremlin medical centre, will also take part along with other top specialists.
It had been widely expected that the operation would be led by Akchurin, who trained in Houston under DeBakey, the 88-year-old patriarch of heart surgery.
DeBakey said last week he thought Yeltsin's operation -- which doctors expect to be a triple bypass -- would take place early this week and the doctors' council on Monday might set a firm date.
Interfax news agency said the doctors would meet at the Barvikha country residence and sanatorium where Yeltsin has been staying for the last few weeks.
Yeltsin, 65, said on September 5 that he had decided to undergo the operation to be able to return to active life.
Preparation for the surgery has been complicated by other health problems and took longer than originally expected.
